story: Qat was born when his father, a stone, exploded. He had eleven brothers, all called Tagaro (Tagaro the Foolish, Tagaro the Wise, and so on), and a companion, Marawa, who could take the form of a spider. Qat created islands and filled them with plants and animals. He carved the first three pairs of men and women from dracaena wood and brought them to life by playing drums and making them dance. Marawa, envious, carved his own figures, brought them to life, then buried them for a week; when dug up they had rotted, and this is how death began. When his brothers tired of endless daylight, Qat created Night and taught them to sleep, later slicing through Night with red obsidian to make Dawn. One day Qat found sky maidens bathing after removing their wings; he hid one pair so that a girl named Vinmara had to stay, becoming his wife, later called Ro-Lei. Qat's mother made her cry, her tears washed away the earth hiding her wings, and she flew off. Qat shot a roped arrow into a banyan tree in the sky and climbed after her, but the root snapped and he fell to his death, while she escaped. Other versions say he sailed away instead, promising to return, or that he climbed a nutmeg tree to escape his hostile brothers, the tree growing endlessly until Marawa blew him a thread to descend. In the most popular version, Qat built a canoe with Marawa's help; his brothers stole it, sailed to another island, and together they defeated a giant named Qasavara.
blind: The hero was born when his father, a stone, exploded. He had several brothers, all sharing one title with different epithets (one foolish, one wise, and so on), and a companion, a trickster spirit who could take the form of a spider. The hero created islands and filled them with plants and animals. He carved the first three pairs of men and women from a sacred type of wood and brought them to life by playing drums and making them dance. The trickster companion, envious, carved his own figures, brought them to life, then buried them for a week; when dug up they had rotted, and this is how death began. When his brothers tired of endless daylight, the hero created Night and taught them to sleep, later slicing through Night with a piece of red volcanic glass to make Dawn. One day the hero found sky maidens bathing after removing their wings; he hid one pair so that one maiden had to stay, becoming his wife, later given another name. The hero's mother made her cry, her tears washed away the earth hiding her wings, and she flew off. The hero shot a roped arrow into a great tree reaching into the sky and climbed after her, but the root snapped and he fell to his death, while she escaped. Other versions say he sailed away instead, promising to return, or that he climbed a tall fruit tree to escape his hostile brothers, the tree growing endlessly until his companion blew him a thread to descend. In the most popular version, the hero built a canoe with his companion's help; his brothers stole it, sailed to another island, and together they defeated a giant.
title: Qat (deity)
